 All Salem High School football players, staff released from hospital after bus crash, district says 
 One person was airlifted for their injuries, according to the district. By Atlanta News First staff Published : Oct. 24, 2026 at 7:31 AM EDT | Updated : 11 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — All 22 students and three adults hurt when a bus carrying Salem High School’s football team overturned have been released from the hospital, Rockdale County Public Schools said.
 The crash remains under investigation.
 The accident happened at the intersection of SR 138 and I-20 at around 10:45 p.m. Friday, according to Georgia State Patrol. Troopers said the bus’s 74-year-old driver was trying to make a right turn onto SR 138 after exiting I-20 eastbound when he lost control.
 The bus crossed the highway’s southbound and northbound lanes, hitting a Kia Soul driven by a 35-year-old Covington man, before rolling over on the side of the road, troopers said.
 One student was airlifted, while the others were taken to multiple hospitals. In total, 27 people were on the bus, Conyers police said: 17 players, seven trainers, two coaches and one driver.
 Rockdale County Superintendent Stephanie Johnson said school and district staff responded to support the injured at hospitals including Grady Memorial Hospital, Piedmont Rockdale Hospital, Children’s Healthcare of Atlanta and facilities in Newton and Walton counties.
 The team was returning from an away game against Greater Atlanta Christian School. The Youth Peace and Justice Foundation said it will provide chaplain support and mental health resources.
 “We are grateful to the first responders, medical professionals, and school and district staff members who cared for our students and adults,” the district said.
